text: The rwb-partner slice of the interaction ledger is the producer of the partner facts: the question does not correspond to a ledger row, a ledger operation or a ledger table in rwb_partner, and the story serves the ledger by stating what a hand-over to a partner and a partner result are, so it is not stated against a table.
why: The ledger is rwb-source-data's by the default ruling (DP-18) and the Ownership Map gives S9 no interaction table, so a statement against a table would be claimed by the wrong service.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-18; context pack S9 ownership rows; legacy RWB-E2-034 sections 11 and 12.
impact: No ledger table, no ledger read and no ledger row in this schema; the entries are written downstream from the fact.

text: No ledger attribute or payload property of this story is invented as a fact: what the story states is the mapping and the handling of the partner channel, and the payload of EV-20 and EV-21 carries the seven ledger attributes only as the contract of RWB-P2-E2034-CON is baselined to name them, with any property that contract does not publish left out of the build.
why: No source publishes the property list of EV-20 or EV-21, and inventing property names as content would put values into the service that the contract does not hold.
read: TSD S9 T5.3; context pack events EV-20 and EV-21; legacy RWB-E2-034 section 12; sibling RWB-S9-E6033-APP section 12.3.
impact: The payload is fixed with the contract owner before build; a property the contract drops is dropped from the fact and no code change of this service is needed.

text: The platform contracts that DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-08, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19 name arrive with the service template, so the metadata row Depends on (build) stays None as the Work Package fixes it and Contract dependencies stays RWB-P2-E2034-CON; the authorise, parameters and reference-data contracts consumed by this slice are class C in fact and are not written into either row.
why: The plan gives this secondary slice an empty H row and one C row, while the DP table of the pattern set adds ten platform or cross-service dependencies.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; split plan story line RWB-S9-E2034-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner; sibling story RWB-S8-E2033-APP section 13.
confirm: Solution architect; platform library owners (RWB-PLT-E1027, E1042, E1043, E1037, TE006, E1071, E1044, N001)
impact: Ready to start stays Day 1; the platform contracts are tracked by their own stories and not by this lane.

text: The event code, the channel, the direction and the source of a partner fact are list rows read at the version in force through the reference-data contract of rwb-case: HANDOVER for an issued instruction and PARTNER_RESULT for a partner result, PORTAL for both, OUTBOUND for a hand-over and INBOUND for a result, WORKBENCH for both, as the legacy business rules fix them; a member whose list has no row is refused rather than defaulted.
why: DP-07 moves lists of values to rwb-case, the legacy story names its lists without publishing their rows, and the guardrail forbids a code in source.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 BR1, BR2, BR4 and section 12; TSD S9 T3.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07; context pack naming rules.
impact: A new value is a data change in rwb-case; a member without a row refuses the fact instead of sending a code the ledger cannot read.

text: The holder references of the fact take the form USER:<identity reference> for the bank holder and PARTNER:<partner_code> for the firm, both as references and never as names; the bank reference comes from the cached access decision and the firm reference from partner.partner_code, as the legacy criterion's values show them.
why: The legacy criterion prints USER:U-2001 and PARTNER:LF-SYN-01 without publishing a format rule, and no source gives the reference element of the access decision or the partner element.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 AC2, BR2 and section 11; TSD S9 T3.1 DF-PRT-002; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 (s17).
impact: The form is one function of the assembler; a change of form changes the contract, the ledger mapping and one test.

text: The retry bound after which a refused fact goes to rwb.partner.events.v1.dlt with a task for role RW-PLATADM is a parameter row of rwb-case, with 3 as the value in force because the legacy story names three retries; no parameter name is published and no bound is written in code.
why: The legacy exception path retries three times and DP-06 requires a changeable value to be a parameter row, while no source names the parameter.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 X5, AC8 and BR8; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06; TSD S9 T5.3.
impact: A bound change is a data change in rwb-case and no release of this service.

text: The contact point is not carried by this service at all: partner_instruction holds no contact column and S9 holds no v_ace_* grant, so the fact carries the instruction, the case, the partner and its code, and the ledger resolves the contact reference through rwb-source-data; the legacy rule that stores the contact point as a reference and never copies it is thus met by omission.
why: The legacy story stores contact_key from v_ace_contact, while TSD S9 T3.1 has no such field and DP-05 confines the ACE reads to rwb-source-data.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 BR5, AC1 and section 11 (DF-ACE-075 to DF-ACE-077); TSD S9 T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05 and DP-18.
confirm: rwb-source-data ledger owner; Compliance and PDPA officer
impact: No personal data leaves the service in a fact; the ledger shows the contact point only when the owner resolves the reference.

text: The twelve legacy test cases keep their identifiers and their legacy order, with a Level column added: legacy System maps to Component for a single-service half, legacy Access maps to Component, and a case whose behaviour belongs to the ledger, the letters or the payments after the split is listed with no criterion here.
why: The legacy table publishes only the ID, the coverage and the data, and the split leaves six of the twelve cases with another owner.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-034 section 16; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 (s16); sibling story RWB-S8-E2033-APP section 16.
impact: The same identifiers run in one service or in the integration harness; no case is lost and none is duplicated.

text: This story adds one step to the per-service Flyway sequence of rwb_partner: a read-only view v_partner_ledger_fact over partner_instruction and partner with one index on the case and the instructed time; no business table, column or constraint is added and no migration of this service touches another schema, and the view and index names are this story's design choice.
why: DP-15 is in the pattern set of the legacy key, the fact is derived from rows two other steps write, and no source names a view over the partner instruction.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15; TSD S9 T3.1 and T3.3; context pack tables partner and partner_instruction.
impact: One migration file in the service's own sequence; the schema keeps three business tables and gains no column.

text: No approval stop is taken: the FSD S9 is In review and the legacy story Ready for build, so the story is drafted at status Draft (realignment v1) and the change is confirmed at the contract review of RWB-P2-E2034-CON and the build review of this service.
why: The realignment run proceeds without human approval and records the missing status as an assumption instead of stopping.
read: FSD S9 document control; legacy RWB-E2-034 metadata (Status: Ready for build); root AGENTS.md rules 9 and 13.
impact: The story is buildable on Day 1 against the contract fakes; a status change does not change its content.
